'''Currarino syndrome'''  is an inherited [[congenital disorder]] where either the [[sacrum]] (the fused vertebrae forming the back of the [[pelvis]]) is not formed properly, or there is a mass in the [[presacral space]] in front of the sacrum, and there are malformations of the [[Human anus|anus]] or [[rectum]]. It occurs in approximately 1 in 100,000 people.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weber |first=Stefanie |last2=Dávila |first2=Magdalena |date=2014 |title=German approach of coding rare diseases with ICD-10-GM and Orpha numbers in routine settings |journal=Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases |volume=9 |issue=Suppl 1 |pages=O10 |doi=10.1186/1750-1172-9-s1-o10 |issn=1750-1172 |pmc=4249588 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Anterior sacral meningocele is the most common presacral mass in patients with Currarino syndrome, occurring in 60% of cases. Its presence may significantly affect the surgical management of these patients.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Emans |first=Pieter J. |last2=van Aalst |first2=Jasper |last3=van Heurn |first3=Ernest L.W. |last4=Marcelis |first4=Carlo |last5=Kootstra |first5=Gauke |last6=Beets-Tan |first6=Regina G.H. |last7=Vles |first7=Johannes S.H. |last8=Beuls |first8=Emile A.M. |date=2006-05-01 |title=The Currarino Triad: Neurosurgical Considerations |journal=Neurosurgery |volume=58 |issue=5 |pages=924–929 |doi=10.1227/01.neu.0000209945.87233.6a |issn=0148-396X |pmid=16639328 |s2cid=45316326}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Samuel |first=M. |last2=Hosie |first2=G. |last3=Holmes |first3=K. |date=December 2000 |title=Currarino triad—Diagnostic dilemma and a combined surgical approach |journal=Journal of Pediatric Surgery |volume=35 |issue=12 |pages=1790–1794 |citeseerx=10.1.1.603.4599 |doi=10.1053/jpsu.2000.19258 |issn=0022-3468 |pmid=11101738}}</ref> Other potential presacral masses include presacral [[teratoma]] and enteric cyst. Presacral [[teratoma]] usually is considered to be a variant of [[sacrococcygeal teratoma]].  However, the presacral teratoma that is characteristic of the Currarino syndrome may be a distinct kind.<ref name="pmid17638164">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Gopal M, Turnpenny PD, Spicer R |date=June 2007 |title=Hereditary sacrococcygeal teratoma--not the same as its sporadic counterpart! |journal=Eur J Pediatr Surg |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=214–6 |doi=10.1055/s-2007-965121 |pmid=17638164 |s2cid=260135903}}</ref>

==Genetics==
[[Image:Autosomal dominant - en.svg|thumb|160 px|right|Currarino syndrome has an autosomal dominant pattern of [[heredity|inheritance]]]]
The disorder is an [[autosomal]] [[dominance (genetics)|dominant]] genetic trait<ref name="pmid4418917">{{Cite journal |last=Ashcraft KW |last2=Holder TM |date=October 1974 |title=Hereditary presacral teratoma |journal=J. Pediatr. Surg. |volume=9 |issue=5 |pages=691–7 |doi=10.1016/0022-3468(74)90107-9 |pmid=4418917}}</ref> caused by a mutation in the [[HLXB9]] homeobox gene. In 2000 the first large series of  Currarino cases was genetically screened for HLXB9 mutations, and it was shown that the gene is specifically causative for the syndrome, but not for other forms of [[sacral agenesis]]. The study was published in the ''[[American Journal of Human Genetics]]''.<ref name="pmid10631160">{{Cite journal |last=Belloni |first=E |last2=Martucciello, G |last3=Verderio, D |last4=Ponti, E |last5=Seri, M |last6=Jasonni, V |last7=Torre, M |last8=Ferrari, M |last9=Tsui, LC |last10=Scherer, SW |date=January 2000 |title=Involvement of the HLXB9 homeobox gene in Currarino syndrome. |journal=American Journal of Human Genetics |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=312–9 |doi=10.1086/302723 |pmc=1288336 |pmid=10631160}}</ref>

==Diagnosis==
Diagnosis of Currarino syndrome is usually clinical, detecting all three elements of the triad. However, [[genetic testing]] is often used as the confirmation of diagnosis and genetic analysis of patient's family members.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=AbouZeid |first=Amr Abdelhamid |last2=Mohammad |first2=Shaimaa Abdelsattar |last3=Abolfotoh |first3=Mohammad |last4=Radwan |first4=Ahmed Bassiouny |last5=Ismail |first5=Mohamed Mohamed ElSayed |last6=Hassan |first6=Tarek Ahmed |date=August 2017 |title=The Currarino triad: What pediatric surgeons need to know |journal=Journal of Pediatric Surgery |language=en |volume=52 |issue=8 |pages=1260–1268 |doi=10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2016.12.010 |pmid=28065719}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Garcia-Barceló |first=Mercè |last2=So |first2=Man-ting |last3=Lau |first3=Danny Ko-chun |last4=Leon |first4=Thomas Yuk-yu |last5=Yuan |first5=Zheng-wei |last6=Cai |first6=Wei-song |last7=Lui |first7=Vincent Chi-hang |last8=Fu |first8=Ming |last9=Herbrick |first9=Jo-Anne |last10=Gutter |first10=Emily |last11=Proud |first11=Virginia |date=2006-01-01 |title=Population Differences in the Polyalanine Domain and 6 New Mutations in HLXB9 in Patients with Currarino Syndrome |journal=Clinical Chemistry |language=en |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=46–52 |doi=10.1373/clinchem.2005.056192 |issn=0009-9147 |pmid=16254195 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Treatment==

Surgery of an anterior [[myelomeningocele]] is  only indicated in the rare case in which the space-occupying aspect is expected to cause constipation or problems during pregnancy or delivery. Fistulas between the spinal canal and colon have to be operated on directly.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Emans PJ, van Aalst J, van Heurn EL, Marcelis C, Kootstra G, Beets-Tan RG, Vles JS, Beuls EA |year=2006 |title=The Currarino triad: neurosurgical considerations |journal=Neurosurgery |volume=58 |issue=5 |pages=924–9; discussion 924–9 |doi=10.1227/01.NEU.0000209945.87233.6A |pmid=16639328 |s2cid=45316326}}</ref>

Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary assessment is recommended to plan adequate treatment.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Samuel M, Hosie G, Holmes K |date=Dec 2000 |title=Currarino triad--diagnostic dilemma and a combined surgical approach |journal=J Pediatr Surg |volume=35 |issue=12 |pages=1790–4 |citeseerx=10.1.1.603.4599 |doi=10.1053/jpsu.2000.19258 |pmid=11101738}}</ref>

By accurate evaluation, the correct surgical management, including neurosurgery, can be performed in a single-stage approach.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Crétolle C, Zérah M, Jaubert F, Sarnacki S, Révillon Y, Lyonnet S, Nihoul-Fékété C |year=2006 |title=New clinical and therapeutic perspectives in Currarino syndrome (study of 29 cases) |journal=J Pediatr Surg |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=126–31; discussion 126–31 |doi=10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2005.10.053 |pmid=16410121}}</ref>

The management of Currarino syndrome is similar to the usual management of anorectal malformation (ARM) regarding the surgical approach and probably the prognosis, which mainly depends on degree of associated sacral dysplasia.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=AbouZeid AA, Mohammad SA, Abolfotoh M, Radwan AB, Ismail MME, Hassan TA |year=2017 |title=The Currarino triad: What pediatric surgeons need to know |journal=J Pediatr Surg |volume=52 |issue=8 |pages=1260–1268 |doi=10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2016.12.010 |pmid=28065719}}</ref>
